newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian mailmen strike, unrest in public sector.
newsitem.headline: Belgian mailmen strike, unrest in public sector.

text.p: Mail delivery was disrupted in parts of Belgium on Friday as postal service staff halted work, angry over management failure to deal with staff shortages and government plans to rein in spending on pensions.
Union concern that pensions will be hit in the drive by the government to cut debt and the budget deficit in the run-up to Europe's single currency will spark further public sector strikes next week.
The 24-hour postal strike called by the main ACOD union representing more than half the Post Office's 45,000 workers began at 2000 GMT on Thursday.
The strike focused on sorting centres, but selected post offices also remained closed. Money transport was affected, while state pension cheques were not being delivered.
In Brussels one in five mailmen worked. In the western town of Ghent 60 percent of staff was on strike, affecting delivery for a third of its inhabitants, the socialist ACOD said.
Liberal and christian unions did not participate in the strike, saying they wanted to wait for the result of negotiations on a new collective agreement.
The CGSP union of public sector workers said the strike was the first in a week of action including a one-hour rail stoppage on Wednesday and a mass rally on Thursday.
